chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'I am traveling and the prayer time arrives, and I fear the dust (ramda') on my face; what should I do?' He said, 'Prostrate on part of your garment.' I said, 'I do not have a garment on which I can prostrate on its edge or its hem.' He said, 'Prostrate on the back of your hand, for it is one of the places of prostration.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for prostration if one fears dust on their face while traveling?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in the conditions of prostration during travel, specifically addressing the concern of dust (ramda') affecting the face. It establishes a hierarchy of valid surfaces, moving from garments to the hand itself, affirming that the back of the hand serves as a legitimate 'place of prostration' (masjid) when other options are unavailable. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (taysir) in ritual purity and prayer mechanics during journeys.
